title: Run native A/B comparisons on examples from real work

intentCoverage.report:
Dough Intent Coverage — SEED-346#run-native-ab-comparisons-on-real-work

Verdict: Caught.

Story and revision: SEED-346#run-native-ab-comparisons-on-real-work (.planning/seeds/SEED-346-native-ab-comparisons.md), revision 8d4c6f3085816f6f32721c3d8baefdea611eb537 on claude/run-native-a-b-comparisons-on-examples-from-real.

Promise checked: Scope "Assessment judges observed state and decisive proof before effort; fewer requests cannot hide a missed decision, fault or restored pass", with key example 3 "An arm missing any decisive result cannot win solely through lower effort" (and example 2's "A baseline's failure remains a comparison result"). The caller's suggested promise, fault area and focused command held and were used unchanged.

Fault: Distribution/tests/support/native-comparison-verdict.sh, native_comparison_judge, `passed/failed)` branch. Inserted, before the `regressed` verdict:
  if (( $(pair_field candidate-commands) < $(pair_field baseline-commands) )); then
    native_comparison_verdict preserved 'the candidate kept the outcome with fewer commands'; return 0
  fi
i.e. a candidate whose case assessment failed is judged `preserved` (status pass) when it used fewer commands. Fixtures, assertions and the substitute host were left intact.

Independent wrong-behavior witness: sourced the faulted judge in a separate bash on a hand-written pair observation (frozen payloads, all conditions same, both complete, baseline-assessment passed, candidate-assessment failed, candidate 7 vs baseline 12 commands). Faulted judge: status=pass outcome=preserved, effort-standing "compared after an outcome the candidate kept". The original judge (restored copy) on the same observation: status=fail outcome=regressed. So the fault makes lower effort hide a missed decision/proof on the intended path.

Maintained check and catch: Distribution/tests/native-comparison-pairs.sh via `PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH bash scripts/test.sh Distribution/tests/native-comparison-pairs.sh`. The substitute pair fixture copies the working-tree harness (including the judge) into its own committed repository, so the faulted judge ran in the entry. The "shortcut" candidate pair (pushes its branch and skips proof, spends fewer commands) is judged by the faulted judge; the run failed with
  FAIL: Distribution/tests/native-comparison-pairs.sh
  stopped at Distribution/tests/native-comparison-pairs.sh:65: grep -Fqx 'verdict: regressed' "${regressed}"
Catching assertion: native-comparison-pairs.sh:65 (the shortcut journey's `verdict: regressed`). Claim limited to that path: a substitute-host sequential pair where the candidate's assessment failed with fewer commands. The judge's counterexample row `cheaper-candidate-missed-proof` (native-comparison-verdict-counterexamples.sh:31) is aimed at the same fault but was not reached in this run, because set -e stopped the script at line 65; no verdict is claimed for it.

Run observations:
- Setup: `git worktree add --detach` of 8d4c6f30 at /Users/terryyin/.claude/jobs/92cad1b7/tmp/ic-scratch; pre-probe state clean (0 porcelain entries), HEAD 8d4c6f30. No npm ci was needed.
- Baseline: rc=0 (quiet pass), about 20.7 s wall, consistent with running the substitute pairs. Reach was shown by the faulted run failing at the pair journey's verdict assertion.
- Faulted: rc=1 at line 65 as above, about 21.2 s wall.
- Restoration: an EXIT trap copied back the pre-probe copy of the judge; `cmp` showed it identical; scratch `git status --porcelain` empty; HEAD unchanged. Restored rerun rc=0 (quiet pass), about 21.2 s wall. Scratch worktree then removed with `git worktree remove` (no longer listed).
- Execution checkout: never edited by this probe; HEAD still 8d4c6f30. When the probe finished it had 4 modified files that were not there at invocation start: .planning/NORTH-STAR.md, .planning/PRODUCT-BACKLOG.md, .planning/slice-plans/621-close-native-comparison-harness-gaps/PLAN.md, Distribution/tests/native-comparison.md. They are presumably concurrent Story Wrap Up edits and were left as they were.

Next proof action: none required for this promise on the observed path. The maintained shortcut-pair assertion catches the "effort decides a failed candidate" fault. Optional: to see the counterexample row's own catch separately, run it without the earlier journey stopping the script first. That is a test-design choice for the caller and is not prompted by any gap.

Prior dispositions: this matches the judge's existing design comment and counterexample intent ("lower effort cannot offset a missed decision or proof"). No new repair is prompted by this probe.

Costs:
- Test runtime: measured, wall-clock milliseconds from host clock around each scripts/test.sh invocation: baseline 20,711 ms; faulted 21,195 ms; restored 21,176 ms (about 63.1 s total). The runner printed no runtime of its own on quiet pass.
- Human effort: unavailable; no human interaction occurred or was measured during this delegated probe (0 known interventions).
- Agent effort: unavailable as a token/cost figure because this agent cannot read its own usage. Observable proxy: about 12 tool calls, measured by count in this run.


- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 138933 ms (measured), from 1794642703844 to 1794642842777 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.

---

Wrap-up disposition (checked revision 8d4c6f3085816f6f32721c3d8baefdea611eb537): verdict Caught; no actionable finding. Evidence: the faulted judge failed `Distribution/tests/native-comparison-pairs.sh:65` and the restored judge passed. Decision: no follow-up; the optional separate run of the `cheaper-candidate-missed-proof` counterexample row is a test-design choice not prompted by a gap, so none is queued. One probe protects only this promise on the observed path, not the whole story. Canonical follow-up for this story's other findings: SEED-346#close-native-comparison-harness-gaps (retrospective, queued first).
